To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount of time a rat allocates to a given duration of responding during generalization depends on the similarity between the test stimulus and the stimulus controlling that duration.

1) a gradient of stimulus generalization reflects a continuous change in the probability of responding; 2) the probability of responding is a function of both the stimulus and response durations present during conditioning; 3) the amount of time rats allocate to a given response is a function of the proximity of the generalization test stimuli to the training stimulus controlling that particular response duration; and 4) stimulus generalization is a result of a continuous change in responding.
the temporal distribution of behavior is determined by the stimulus conditions present during training and that the stimulus control of response duration is not a unitary function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how animals learn to allocate their time to various activities.
the analysis of stimulus control in terms of response topography and the temporal allocation of responding.
the development of an experimental approach for the analysis of the stimulus control of behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stimulus control is not a unitary phenomenon, but is a function of many variables.
the results of this experiment are consistent with the hypothesis that a gradient of control is a function of the similarity between the test and training stimuli.
the gradient of responding is not a function of the similarity between test and training stimuli, but of the similarity between the training stimuli and those present during the test.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal organization of a response depends not on the temporal characteristics of the response per se, but on the stimulus controlling the response.
the temporal allocation of behavior to stimulus defined durations is a function of the stimulus control of the response durations.
stimulus control is a function of the temporal distribution of reinforcement and the response duration distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gradient of stimulus control can be used as a tool to understand the mechanisms of stimulus control, and that it is possible to control responding in a temporally defined manner by using gradients of stimuli.
stimulus control can be understood in terms of a gradient of stimulus generalization, but that generalization gradients are not the only determinant of the allocation of time to behavior.
the allocation of time to a particular duration depends on the similarity of the test stimulus (i.e., the light intensity) to the training stimulus (i.e. light intensity).
